documents.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies for Instructional and Assignment Purposes
documents.summary: Board policy that defines AI and generative AI, sets user duties (privacy, accuracy, bias, copyright, disclosure) and bans fabrication. It leaves detailed rules on student and faculty use to the Provost's guidance and to departments or instructors.
documents.stance_why: The policy bans only fabricating data or falsifying academic content ('strictly prohibited') and says use is 'permitted under this policy' without saying when; it directs the Provost to publish guidance and says 'The department or instructor of record may also establish policies'. It sets no course-level stance of its own, so delegates.

units.why: The purpose statement says the policy 'specifies East Tennessee State University's (ETSU or University) approach' to AI by faculty, staff and students, so it is an institution-level framework (P56) rather than a rule about a single use.
units.anchor: approach to the use of artificial intelligence by ETSU faculty, staff, and students

units.why: 'This policy is applicable to ETSU faculty, staff, and students' sets the scope of the framework, so it is a scope statement under P56; P61 is for definitions of AI, which this is not.
units.anchor: This policy is applicable to ETSU faculty, staff, and students.

units.why: The Board committee 'is responsible for the review and revision of this policy', which assigns maintenance of the policy, so it belongs under revisiting the policy (P54).
units.anchor: responsible for the review and revision of this policy

units.why: The definition of 'Artificial Intelligence Technologies' sets what the policy covers, so it is a definition/scope unit (P61).
units.anchor: Machine-based system s that can, for a given set of human -defined objectives, make predictions,

units.why: The definition of 'Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI)' as systems 'capable of creating new content' fixes the scope of the rules that follow, so P61.
units.anchor: Artificial intelligence systems that are capable of creating new content or data

units.why: The definition of 'Regulated Data' (SSNs, HIPAA, FERPA records) sets what data the later privacy rules protect; it is a scope definition (P61), with the privacy rules themselves coded under P50.
units.anchor: Information that is protected by laws and regulations that restrict how it can be used

units.why: ETSU 'recognizes the potential benefits of the responsible use' of AI but is 'aware of its limitations and the potential risks'; this is a preamble of principles (P56), not an operative default, so P02 does not fit.
units.anchor: recognizes the potential benefits of the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies

units.why: Using AI 'to fabricate data or research results, or to falsify academic content is strictly prohibited'; a flat ban on a specific misuse that none of the closed types covers (it is not P19, which is about submitting AI-made work as one's own).
units.anchor: to fabricate data or research results, or to falsify academic content is strictly prohibited
units.uncovered_note: Strict ban on using AI to fabricate data or research results or falsify academic content.

units.why: The Provost 'will publish written guidance and University policies' on GAI for faculty and students, so the Board policy hands detail to an administrative office; this is institution-level set-up (P56).
units.anchor: the Office of the Provost will publish written guidance and University policies, as needed

units.why: 'Staff assisting faculty ... will follow the same requirements as faculty' extends the policy's scope to support staff, so it is a scope statement (P61).
units.anchor: Staff assisting faculty with their course design, preparation, or with student support of a course

units.why: 'The department or instructor of record may also establish policies' means the permission rule is set per department or instructor, which is P04.
units.anchor: The department or instructor of record may also establish policies

units.why: Local policies are 'not to supersede or conflict with this Board policy or University policy', a hierarchy rule for who prevails; coded P56 (framework) since P04 is about the freedom to decide.
units.anchor: not to supersede or conflict with this Board policy or University policy

units.why: Local policies 'must be in writing and in a format accessible to students', which requires instructors to communicate their AI rule in writing (P09).
units.anchor: these policies must be in writing and in a format accessible to students

units.why: Users 'Shall follow all University and department policies related to the use and academic misconduct'; a general duty to comply with other policies, filed under the framework type P56.
units.anchor: Shall follow all University and department policies related to the use and academic misconduct

units.why: Users 'Shall not input Confidential Data or Regulated Data' into GAI, a data-protection rule (P50).
units.anchor: Shall not input Confidential Data or Regulated Data into or use GAI

units.why: Users 'Shall immediately report' any breach or suspected breach of data to IT Services, a data-protection duty under P50.
units.anchor: Shall immediately report a ny Breach or suspected Breach of data

units.why: Users 'Shall not utilize GAI to present a work as their own in violation of another individual's intellectual property rights'; this is about IP, so P52 rather than P19.
units.anchor: Shall not utilize GAI to present a work as their own in violation of another

units.why: 'Shall follow all copyright laws' is a copyright compliance rule (P52).
units.anchor: Shall follow all copyright laws

units.why: Users 'Shall not utilize GAI to create malicious content (e.g., malware, viruses...)'; a harm-avoidance rule that fits P53 (harms) better than any prohibition type.
units.anchor: Shall not utilize GAI to create malicious content

units.why: Users 'Shall confirm the accuracy of the GAI output received before utilizing the information', i.e. verify AI output (P31).
units.anchor: Shall confirm the accuracy of the GAI output received before utilizing the information

units.why: Users 'Shall consider the potential bias and inaccuracies inherent to GAI, and revise accordingly'; this asks for critical evaluation of output, so P31.
units.anchor: Shall consider the potential bias and inaccuracies inherent to GAI, and revise accordingly

units.why: Users 'Shall disclose the use of GAI', a disclosure requirement (P24).
units.anchor: Shall disclose the use of GAI

units.why: Users 'Shall be responsible for continually consulting University and department policies regarding GAI use, as this technology will continue to evolve'; ties compliance to a changing policy, so P54.
units.anchor: continually consulting University and department policies regarding GAI use

units.why: 'compliance with data protection regulations, such as ... HIPAA ... FERPA ... GDPR ... is mandatory' is a privacy rule (P50).
units.anchor: compliance with data protection regulations

units.why: 'when using AIT, including GAI for grading purposes, personal student data must be de-identified' addresses instructor use of AI for grading, but the operative rule is data protection (P50), not who grades (P46).
units.anchor: when using AIT, including GAI for grading purposes, personal student data must be de- identified

units.why: 'Users are prohibited from inputting identifiable data concerning individuals (students, patients, or others)' is an absolute data-input ban, coded P50.
units.anchor: Users are prohibited from inputting identifiable data concerning individuals

units.why: 'Users ... are expected to engage with the technology in an ethical and responsible manner' states an ethics expectation (P53).
units.anchor: are expected to engage with the technology in an ethical and responsible manner

units.why: 'Avoiding the generation or dissemination of harmful, offensive, or misleading content' is an ethical-harm rule (P53).
units.anchor: Avoiding the generation or dissemination of harmful, offensive, or misleading content

units.why: Use must align 'with the University's values of inclusivity, respect, and academic integrity', an ethics principle (P53).
units.anchor: Ensuring that the use aligns with the University 's values of inclusivity, respect, and academic

units.why: 'Recognizing the limitations and potential biases, particularly when using content generated in decision-making or research' names bias as a concern (P53); it overlaps P31 but is framed as an ethical consideration.
units.anchor: Recognizing the limitations and potential biases, particularly when using content generated in decision-making or research

units.why: 'Violations of this policy will be subject to the University's policies on academic misconduct and/or the University's human resource disciplinary policy' routes violations to misconduct processes (P36).
units.anchor: Violations of this policy will be subject to the University

units.why: 'This policy may only be revised by the Board of Trustees' states who maintains and changes the policy (P54).
units.anchor: This policy may only be revised by the Board of Trustees

documents.unit: Office of the Provost / GAI Task Force
documents.title: Written Guidance for Ethical Use of Generative AI at ETSU
documents.summary: Provost-level guidance with four core principles (disclosure, privacy, human oversight, staying current) and role-specific procedures for students, instructors, researchers and staff. It affirms AI use generally and leaves course permissions to instructors' syllabi.
documents.stance_why: The Task Force 'generally affirms' AI use, but students must 'adhere to the instructor's specified parameters regarding AI use, as stated in the syllabus' and fully AI-generated work is banned only 'unless explicitly permitted by the instructor'. The permission decision sits with instructors, so delegates.

units.why: The Task Force 'generally affirms its use on campus when it can support the work' of faculty, staff and students, a welcoming default tempered by conditions (P02).
units.anchor: generally aﬃrms its use on campus when it can support the work of faculty, staﬀ,

units.why: The guidance 'supplements the ETSU Board of Trustees Policy', stating its purpose and place in the institutional framework (P56).
units.anchor: This written guidance supplements the ETSU Board of Trustees Policy

units.why: Affiliates 'shall do so ethically, respectfully, and responsibly' in line with 'honesty, integrity, inclusivity, and trust'; a principle statement (P56).
units.anchor: shall do so ethically, respectfully, and responsibly

units.why: 'Misuse, including falsifying academic content or research data ..., generating malicious or misleading information, or infringing on intellectual property rights, is strictly prohibited'; a ban on named misuses that no closed type captures.
units.anchor: is strictly prohibited
units.uncovered_note: Strict ban on misuse: falsifying academic content or research data, generating malicious or misleading information, infringing intellectual property.

units.why: Community members 'shall transparently disclose such usage' of generative AI in academic, administrative or research contexts, a general disclosure rule (P24).
units.anchor: shall transparently disclose such usage in a manner that is both appropriate and clear

units.why: It 'includes attributing AI-generated content or substantial Gen AI contributions' for course assignments and publications, which specifies the attribution duty for submissions (P24).
units.anchor: attributing AI-generated content or substantial Gen AI contributions

units.why: 'All uses of generative artificial intelligence must comply with applicable laws and institutional policies governing data privacy' is a privacy rule (P50).
units.anchor: must comply with applicable laws and institutional policies governing data privacy, conﬁdentiality, and security

units.why: 'Users are prohibited from inputting or otherwise exposing confidential or regulated data ... to unauthorized Gen AI platforms' is a data-input ban (P50).
units.anchor: Users are prohibited from inputting or otherwise exposing conﬁdential or regulated data

units.why: AI must be used 'with appropriate human oversight' and individuals 'must carefully review and validate Gen AI outputs', i.e. verify output (P31).
units.anchor: Individuals must carefully review and validate Gen AI outputs against their own knowledge and skills

units.why: 'The ultimate responsibility ... remains with the human user, who is accountable for compliance with all university policies', an ownership/accountability rule (P29).
units.anchor: The ultimate responsibility for verifying the accuracy, fairness, and integrity of AI-generated content or decisions

units.why: Affiliates 'shall maintain ongoing awareness of developments, best practices, and emerging guidelines'; a duty to keep up with AI that no closed type names exactly.
units.anchor: shall maintain ongoing awareness of developments, best practices, and emerging guidelines in Gen AI
units.uncovered_note: Users must keep up to date with developments, best practices and guidelines on generative AI (Core Principle 4).

units.why: Students must 'adhere to the instructor's specified parameters regarding AI use, as stated in the syllabus or assignment instructions', so the instructor sets the rule (P04).
units.anchor: Clearly review and adhere to the instructor’s speciﬁed parameters regarding AI use

units.why: Students must cite generative AI 'whenever generative AI contributes substantially', using the instructor's format or style guides, a disclosure/citation rule (P24).
units.anchor: clearly cite its use according to the instructor-speciﬁed format or standard citation practices

units.why: Students should 'Avoid submitting fully AI-generated content as original work unless explicitly permitted by the instructor', i.e. do not have AI produce the submitted work (P19) with a permit-if-allowed exception.
units.anchor: Avoid submitting fully AI-generated content as original work unless explicitly permitted by the instructor

units.why: 'Submitting such work without clear permission constitutes academic misconduct' classifies unauthorized AI-generated submissions as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Submitting such work without clear permission constitutes academic misconduct

units.why: Students in research 'must obtain IRB approval and explicit consent for any human-subject data processed using AI'; research rules go under P62.
units.anchor: students must obtain IRB approval and explicit consent for any human-subject data processed using AI

units.why: 'Data must always be anonymized before system upload or analysis' for students doing research; a research-data rule (P62), distinct from the IRB duty above.
units.anchor: Data must always be anonymized before system upload or analysis activities

units.why: Students should 'regularly review available university resources to remain current on best practices'; the same keep-up duty as Core Principle 4 applied to students.
units.anchor: Regularly review available university resources to remain current on best practices for responsible AI use
units.uncovered_note: Students review university resources to stay current on responsible AI use.

units.why: Instructors must 'Include explicit statements about acceptable Gen AI usage in course syllabi', a syllabus-statement requirement (P09).
units.anchor: Include explicit statements about acceptable Gen AI usage in course syllabi

units.why: Instructors must 'provide detailed guidelines for individual assignments to prevent ambiguity', so assignment-level rules are expected (P04).
units.anchor: provide detailed guidelines for individual assignments to prevent ambiguity

units.why: Instructors using AI for course materials or feedback must 'Clearly cite any AI involvement and review all AI-generated material', i.e. AI-made materials are disclosed and reviewed (P48).
units.anchor: Clearly cite any AI involvement and review all AI-generated material to ensure accuracy, appropriateness, and

units.why: Instructors must 'De-identify all student work before uploading to Gen AI platforms for feedback or assessment', a privacy rule (P50) on faculty use.
units.anchor: De-identify all student work before uploading to Gen AI platforms for feedback or assessment purposes

units.why: Instructors 'Carefully review and correct AI-generated feedback to ensure accuracy and fairness'; this is what instructors do when using AI in teaching work (P59), not a ban on AI grading.
units.anchor: Carefully review and correct AI- generated feedback to ensure accuracy and fairness

units.why: Instructors investigating misconduct should 'Use multiple evidence sources, including AI detection software, style analysis, and prompt logs', which lists the evidence used to identify misuse (P40).
units.anchor: Use multiple evidence sources, including AI detection software, style analysis, and prompt logs

units.why: 'Do not rely solely on Gen AI-detection scores, which have questionable validity' tells instructors not to treat detectors as proof (P39).
units.anchor: Do not rely solely on Gen AI-detection scores, which have questionable validity

units.why: Instructors should 'engage in institutional training to stay informed about emerging Gen AI practices', which fits supporting faculty in learning AI (P63).
units.anchor: Regularly consult institutional support materials and engage in institutional training

units.why: Researchers must 'Clearly disclose the specific generative AI tools used, their purpose, and methods' in Methods or Acknowledgments, a research-publication rule (P62).
units.anchor: Clearly disclose the speciﬁc generative AI tools used, their purpose, and methods of application

units.why: 'AI should never be credited as an author' is a scholarship authorship rule (P62).
units.anchor: AI should never be credited as an author

units.why: Researchers must 'Secure IRB approval and informed consent before utilizing generative AI to analyze any human-subject data', a research rule (P62).
units.anchor: Secure IRB approval and informed consent before utilizing generative AI to analyze any human-subject data

units.why: Researchers must 'Document all bias checks and verification procedures in lab notebooks or in public registries'; a research-integrity documentation rule (P62) rather than the general verification rule (P31).
units.anchor: Document all bias checks and veriﬁcation procedures in lab notebooks or in public registries

units.why: Researchers should participate in 'research-focused AI training, workshops, or seminars' to stay current; the same keep-up duty as Core Principle 4.
units.anchor: participate in research-focused AI training, workshops, or seminars
units.uncovered_note: Researchers regularly consult materials and take AI training to stay up to date with ethical standards and practices.

units.why: Staff must 'clearly and appropriately disclose' AI use when creating reports and communications and 'verify outputs', a disclosure rule (P24) for staff.
units.anchor: clearly and appropriately disclose its use and verify outputs for accuracy and context

units.why: Staff should 'Utilize AI platforms that protect the handling of confidential or regulated data, thereby avoiding public or unsecured tools', preferring vetted tools (P50).
units.anchor: Utilize AI platforms that protect the handling of conﬁdential or regulated data, thereby avoiding public

units.why: Staff must 'Always remove sensitive details such as personal identifiers' before processing; a data-protection rule (P50).
units.anchor: Always remove sensitive details such as personal identiﬁers or protected ﬁnancial information before processing

units.why: Staff must 'Thoroughly check, verify accuracy, and review the style' of AI-generated documents before dissemination, i.e. verify AI output (P31).
units.anchor: Thoroughly check, verify accuracy, and review the style of any documents or outputs generated using

units.why: Staff should 'Stay updated with institutional training and workshops' to integrate AI in administrative tasks; the keep-up duty of Core Principle 4 for staff.
units.anchor: Stay updated with institutional training and workshops
units.uncovered_note: Staff keep up with institutional training to integrate responsible AI use into administrative tasks.

units.why: The AI Advisory Task Force 'will meet regularly to review this guidance in light of new legal developments', a review cycle (P54).
units.anchor: will meet regularly to review this guidance in light of new legal developments

units.why: 'All revisions to the guidance or procedures will be timestamped and archived', a version-control commitment under revisiting the policy (P54).
units.anchor: All revisions to the guidance or procedures will be timestamped and archived

units.why: 'ETSU will provide regular training, consultations, and digital resources' supports faculty (and others) in learning AI (P63).
units.anchor: ETSU will provide regular training, consultations, and digital resources

units.why: 'Faculty, staff, and students are encouraged to submit feedback or suggestions' invites feedback on the guidance, which is P54.
units.anchor: are encouraged to submit feedback or suggestions via the online form provided

units.why: 'Academic or research misconduct involving AI will be addressed through the university's existing procedures' classes AI misuse under misconduct processes (P36).
units.anchor: Academic or research misconduct involving AI will be addressed through the university

units.why: 'AI detection tools may inform, but cannot solely determine, cases of misconduct' says detectors are not proof (P39).
units.anchor: AI detection tools may inform, but cannot solely determine, cases o f misconduct

units.why: 'All allegations must include human judgment and context-based review' sets fairness in AI-related integrity cases (P64).
units.anchor: All allegations must include human judgment and context-based review

units.why: The Task Force 'is responsible for implementing, reviewing, and revising this set of guidelines', assigning maintenance (P54).
units.anchor: is responsible for implementing, reviewing, and revising this set of guidelines

units.why: The guidance discloses that 'Generative artificial intelligence technologies were utilized to assist in the research, drafting' and that personnel 'carefully reviewed and validated' the content; AI-made institutional material disclosed and reviewed (P48).
units.anchor: carefully reviewed and validated all generative AI content to ensure accuracy, relevance, and compliance

documents.title: Creating a Generative AI Policy for Your Course
tiers: Yellow - Limited use with clear boundaries
documents.summary: Teaching-center step-by-step guide for instructors on writing a course GenAI policy. It offers a red/yellow/green tier model with sample syllabus text for each tier.
documents.stance_why: The guide tells instructors to 'Decide whether to prohibit, limit, or encourage GenAI use in your course' and supplies three tiered templates (Red, Yellow, Green), so it sets no stance itself; delegates with tiers listed.

units.why: 'Every GenAI policy should include the following' lists required syllabus components, so it advises instructors to state AI expectations in the syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: Every GenAI policy should include the following

units.why: Instructors should 'take time to understand how GenAI tools work' before drafting a policy, which supports faculty in learning AI (P63).
units.anchor: take time to understand how GenAI tools work and how they might affect your classroom

units.why: Instructors are told to 'Review ETSU's Written Guidance for Ethical Use of Generative AI' and note its principles, tying course policies to the university guidance (P56).
units.anchor: Review ETSU’s Written Guidance for Ethical Use of Generative AI

units.why: To pick a policy, instructors should 'critically analyze how GenAI could help, hinder, or transform your course LOs'; the course-level choice rests with the instructor (P04).
units.anchor: critically analyze how GenAI could help, hinder, or transform your course LOs

units.why: 'Consider revising LOs to emphasize higher-order thinking, creativity, and critical GenAI literacy' recommends redesigning the course around AI (P35).
units.anchor: Consider revising LOs to emphasize higher-order thinking, creativity, and critical GenAI literacy

units.why: Instructors are asked to 'Consider the Degree of GenAI use' using spectrum diagrams of human vs AI work, i.e. levels of permitted AI use (P05).
units.anchor: Figures 2 & 3 contain diagrams that help you think through which (if any) forms

units.why: 'Consider assigning projects/activities that incorporate GenAI' recommends assignments redesigned around AI (P35).
units.anchor: assigning projects/activities that incorporate GenAI

units.why: 'Decide whether to prohibit, limit, or encourage GenAI use in your course' puts the stance decision with each instructor (P04).
units.anchor: Decide whether to prohibit, limit, or encourage GenAI use in your course

units.why: Red - Prohibit Use: 'GenAI is not allowed. Emphasize development of original thinking and skill-building.' is a named tier of a traffic-light scheme (P05).
units.anchor: Red – Prohibit Use: GenAI is not allowed. Emphasize development of original thinking and skill-building.

units.why: Yellow - Limited Use: 'GenAI may be used for specific tasks (e.g., brainstorming), but not others'; a named middle tier (P05).
units.anchor: GenAI may be used for specific tasks (e.g., brainstorming), but not others

units.why: Green - Encourage with Attribution: 'GenAI is welcomed, with expectations for transparency, reflection, and attribution'; the third named tier (P05).
units.anchor: GenAI is welcomed, with expectations for transparency, reflection, and attribution

units.why: Policies need a 'Definition of GenAI' that states 'what does (not) count as GenAI'; a requirement to define AI for the course's scope (P61).
units.anchor: Your policy should clearly outline what does (not) count as GenAI

units.why: 'Permissible and Prohibited Uses. Be specific and provide examples' tells instructors what the syllabus statement must contain (P09).
units.anchor: Permissible and Prohibited Uses. Be specific and provide examples.

units.why: Policies must outline 'what happens if students use GenAI in ways that don't align with your policy', i.e. state consequences in advance (P37).
units.anchor: Clearly outline what happens if students use GenAI in ways that don’t align with your

units.why: Instructors should 'Emphasize learning and fairness over punishment, and try to keep the tone warm'; a tone/approach for responding to misuse that no closed type names.
units.anchor: Emphasize learning and fairness over punishment, and try to keep the tone warm
units.uncovered_note: Responses to AI misuse should emphasize learning and fairness over punishment and keep a warm tone.

units.why: Recommended component 'Rationale for policy' tells instructors to explain why the rule exists, a syllabus-content recommendation (P09).
units.anchor: Rationale for policy

units.why: 'Encouragement to ask questions' recommends inviting students to ask instructors about AI use (P10).
units.anchor: Encouragement to ask questions

units.why: 'Reminder about GenAI's limitations (e.g., bias, inaccuracy)' recommends warning students that AI output can be wrong (P31).
units.anchor: Reminder about GenAI’s limitations (e.g., bias, inaccuracy)

units.why: 'Guidelines for citation and documentation' recommends telling students how to cite AI use (P24).
units.anchor: Guidelines for citation and documentation

units.why: 'Suggestions for documenting original student work' recommends ways students can evidence their own work, e.g. drafts (P26).
units.anchor: Suggestions for documenting original student work

units.why: The OpenAI-sourced sample definition says tools 'count as Generative AI when they help you generate, rewrite, or complete work' and lists non-GenAI tools; definitional scope (P61).
units.anchor: These tools count as Generative AI when they help you generate, rewrite, or complete work.

units.why: Sample RED: 'GenAI use is not allowed in this course for any activity or assignment' is a blanket default ban (P01).
units.anchor: GenAI use is not allowed in this course for any activity or assignment.

units.why: RED bans 'Submitting any AI-generated content', i.e. AI may not produce submitted work (P19).
units.anchor: Submitting any AI-generated content

units.why: RED bans 'Using GenAI to brainstorm, outline, or revise'; banning brainstorming and outlining fits no closed type (P19 is about producing submitted work).
units.anchor: Using GenAI to brainstorm, outline, or revise
units.uncovered_note: Under the Red policy, no AI for brainstorming, outlining or revising.

units.why: RED bans 'Uploading work to AI tools for feedback or editing', i.e. students may not give their own work to an AI tool (P20).
units.anchor: Uploading work to AI tools for feedback or editing

units.why: RED bans 'Using AI to summarize or analyze readings'; a ban on AI for reading comprehension that no closed type covers.
units.anchor: Using AI to summarize or analyze readings
units.uncovered_note: Under the Red policy, no AI to summarize or analyze readings.

units.why: RED rationale: 'Using GenAI to complete coursework bypasses these learning processes and undermines your independence and skill development' explains that AI shortcuts skill-building practice (P41).
units.anchor: Using GenAI to complete coursework bypasses these learning processes

units.why: RED: 'all assignments must be your own unaided work' requires students to own what they submit (P29).
units.anchor: all assignments must be your own unaided work

units.anchor: may regrettably result in [a reduced grade, the need to revise and resubmit your work,]

units.why: RED reminder: 'ask your instructor before submitting your work' if unsure (P10).
units.anchor: ask your instructor before submitting your work

units.anchor: Basic grammar/spell checkers (e.g., Word editor), search engines, and citation managers are not considered GenAI

units.why: YELLOW: 'You may use GenAI for brainstorming' allows brainstorming (P15).
units.anchor: You may use GenAI for brainstorming

units.anchor: you are required to disclose any and all use of GenAI in course assignments
